launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

_doc_vendored_engine: CI does NOT run the engine source in 1_cicd/src/scripts — it runs the VENDORED COPY at ./build.sh, from this directory. This key DECLARES that copy relationship so the workflow generator can enforce byte-identity (cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh, step 'verify engine ↔ vendored build.sh parity') and go red on drift. Editing the engine alone used to change nothing at ship time, silently — which is how the ABI gate and the GHCR auto-delete gate came to exist only in the file nobody executes. Re-sync with: cp 1_cicd/src/scripts/<engine> ./build.sh
name: cloud-gallery
description: Cloud Gallery — a photo/video gallery app forked from IacobIonut01/ReFra (ex-com.diegonmarcos.mediacenter). Single-app fork (NOT a hub+forks constellation like ea_cloud-comms/ac_cloud-ide): one APK, one materialized upstream tracker. Extends the upstream local MediaStore gallery with two additional non-local media sources behind the SAME Album/MediaItem model: an HTTP 'manifest' source (WG-gated JSON index + thumbs, also used to mirror Instagram via a server-side gallery-dl job) and a 'newpipe' source (NewPipeExtractor, YouTube only). See data/media-profiles.json for the profile registry — Kotlin iterates it, never a hardcoded source list.
_doc_mode: Engine data-signal (cloud-comms-fork-engine.sh) opting this app OUT of the hub+bundle-forks+IPC-contract model used by ea_cloud-{mail,chat,dialer,matrix}. Absence of this key (their build.json shape) means the engine's original hub-coupled steps run unchanged; 'single-app' means the engine builds+signs the one forks.<key> entry directly via the existing step_build_fork machinery.

android._doc_min_sdk: 29, not 26 used by ac_cloud-ide/nav/mail — inherited as-is from upstream ReFra's own minSdk (verified 2026-07-26 against app/build.gradle.kts on main; a prior scaffold pass fabricated 30). Lowering it would require patching upstream Compose/media APIs we don't intend to touch.
android._doc_abi_filters: NOT CONSUMED BY THIS APP — schema parity only. aa_cloud-superapp and ab_cloud-libs-shared/* read build.json::android.abi_filters from their gradle files; nothing under ac_cloud-gallery does. This app inherits upstream ReFra's `flavorDimensions += "abi"` axis (app/build.gradle.kts::productFlavors), and the shipped ABI is chosen per matrix job by COMMS_BUNDLE_ABI, which build.sh maps to the matching assemble task via build.gradle_task_by_abi. Listing only arm64-v8a here was therefore inert AND false: release.abis and release.variants both ship arm64-v8a + x86_64, and `unzip -l` on the published assets confirms lib/arm64-v8a/ and lib/x86_64/ respectively. Kept in sync with release.abis so the two cannot disagree again.

license._doc: Upstream ReFra (ex-Gallery) is Apache-2.0. OUR fork is GPL-3.0 for the whole app, NOT Apache-2.0, because we statically link com.github.teamnewpipe:NewPipeExtractor (GPL-3.0, pulled via JitPack for the 'newpipe' YouTube source — see data/media-profiles.json::profiles[youtube]). GPL-3.0 is a stricter copyleft than Apache-2.0; combining a GPL-3.0 dependency into the app requires the resulting APK/derivative work to be distributed under GPL-3.0 terms. This is a DECIDED relicense, not an oversight — record it verbatim in README.md and in the app's about/licenses screen once implemented.
license.relicense_reason: GPL-3.0 copyleft dependency (NewPipeExtractor) pulled into the app for the YouTube 'newpipe' media source

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, Cloud-IDE, Cloud-SuperApp, and now Cloud-Gallery). Same key so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig (or a written keystore.properties for the upstream tracker) reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD telling you to use the one shared key — it never generates or substitutes a random/legacy key. Copied verbatim from ac_cloud-mail/build.json::signing.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility, mirrored in flake.nix — keep in sync. Same AGP/Gradle/Kotlin/JDK pins as ac_cloud-ide / ac_cloud-nav so all constellation Android projects share one toolchain story. NOTE: the fork itself builds via its OWN gradlew (see fork.build below) which may pin different AGP/Gradle versions upstream — this toolchain block covers OUR devShell tooling (adb/jq/oras/gh), not necessarily what actually compiles the fork.
toolchain._doc_ndk: REQUIRED, not optional — verified 2026-07-26 against upstream app/build.gradle.kts: ReFra has externalNativeBuild + CMake, with JNI over libheif/libde265. A prior scaffold pass wrongly assumed this is a pure Kotlin/Compose app with no native code and pinned a stale NDK for schema parity only; that assumption was wrong.
toolchain._doc_cmake: REQUIRED alongside ndk above — CMake version pinned by upstream's build.gradle.kts externalNativeBuild block. Must be kept in sync with flake.nix::androidenv.composeAndroidPackages.cmakeVersions.

diagnostics._doc: Same shape as ac_cloud-ide::diagnostics. Baked into BuildConfig.LOG_SINK_URL / LOG_SINK_STREAM once the fork's build.gradle is patched to read it (not done yet — no patches/ series exists). EMPTY behavior until wired: cloud push disabled. Data-driven — never hardcode in Kotlin.

gallery._doc: Plural 'forks.<key>' map — same shape as ac_cloud-mail/build.json::forks.mail (and chat/dialer/matrix), reconciled 2026-07-26 to match the engine's existing forks-keyed step_build_fork/step_materialize_fork loop instead of a bespoke singular block. This app has exactly one key ('gallery') because it IS the fork (no separate thin hub) — see top-level mode:'single-app'.
gallery.tracker_dir_note: flattened 2026-08-29 — the vendored source now sits at the app root, matching every other app in this repo instead of hiding under upstream/. upstream_repo/pinned_tag stay provenance only; bump pinned_tag + re-run materialize-fork to re-vendor a newer tag.
gallery._doc_pinned_tag: Re-verified 2026-07-26 via GitHub API tag list: there is NO tag literally named '5.1.0' — a prior scaffold pass fabricated it. Real tags (newest first): 5.1.1-51101-nightly, 5.1.0-51005-nightly, 5.1.0-51004-nightly, 5.1.0-51003-nightly, 5.1.0-51002-nightly, 5.1.0-51001-nightly, 5.0.3-50301-nightly, 5.0.2-50201-nightly, 5.0.0-50002-nightly, 4.3.1-43101-nightly, 4.3.0. Upstream ships nightlies as its de facto release channel — there is no recent non-nightly tag; 4.3.0 is the last plain-semver tag. Pinned to the newest tag, 5.1.1-51101-nightly, deviating from house convention (ac_cloud-mail pins a stable FairEmail tag) only because no recent stable tag exists. REVIEW this pin whenever upstream cuts an actual stable release.

build._doc: gradle_task_by_abi VERIFIED against a real GHA build (run 30535280370) plus upstream app/build.gradle.kts. Upstream declares `flavorDimensions += listOf("abi","ml")` and generates one abi flavor per key of `abiVersionCodes` = arm64-v8a / armeabi-v7a / x86_64 / x86 / universal. Gradle capitalizes only the FIRST letter of a flavor name, so the hyphen SURVIVES in the task name: assembleArm64-v8aNoMLRelease, NOT assembleArm64V8aNoMLRelease. Run 30535280370 failed with exactly that: "Task assembleArm64V8aNoMLRelease not found ... Some candidates are: assembleArm64-v8aNoMLRelease". We select the NoML flavor (skips upstream on-device ML models) + Release build type. The engine picks the entry matching COMMS_BUNDLE_ABI, falling back to .gradle_task.
build._doc_ml_asset_pack: Upstream declares an asset pack module `:ml-models` (`assetPacks += listOf(":ml-models")`) alongside the WithML/NoML flavor dimension. UNCONFIRMED: whether the NoML flavor we build still pulls in the :ml-models asset pack at the Gradle Play Asset Delivery level, or whether NoML fully excludes it. Do not assume exclusion — verify against the actual `assembleArm64V8aNoMLRelease` output (and `app/build.gradle.kts` asset-pack wiring) on the first real build before relying on this.
build._doc_gradle_task_legacy: gradle_task retained as the single-ABI fallback and is DEPRECATED for this app; the by_abi map above is authoritative. It is intentionally left pointing at the arm64 task so a build with no COMMS_BUNDLE_ABI set still targets the phone ABI.
build._doc_signing: VERIFIED against upstream app/build.gradle.kts: signingConfigs.release sets storeFile = file("release_key.jks") (relative to the app/ module) and reads storePassword/keyAlias/keyPassword from System.getenv("SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD"/"SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS"/"SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD"). ReFra never reads a keystore.properties — the string "keystore.properties" does not appear anywhere in its gradle files. The previous value "keystore_properties" was copied verbatim from ac_cloud-mail (FairEmail DOES read that file) and made GHA run 30538571570 fail at configure time with: storeFile specifies file .../app/release_key.jks which doesnt exist. storeFile resolves during CONFIGURATION, so the engine must place the keystore before the task graph is built. Still the ONE shared vault key (.signing.vault_keystore) — this only changes DELIVERY, never which key signs.

gallery.comment: ReFra (ex-Gallery, com.diegonmarcos.mediacenter). Pure Kotlin/Compose, no RN/Cordova wrapper — closest in shape to the FairEmail fork (native gradle build, keystore.properties signing), not to the RN/Cordova forks in ea_cloud-comms. No patches/ series exists yet (empty tracker checkout at pinned tag is valid during scaffolding, per cloud-comms-fork-engine.sh::step_materialize_fork's 'no patches yet' path).
gallery._doc_owned: NO LONGER TRACKED UPSTREAM (2026-08-30). The package identity was renamed off com.dot.gallery onto com.diegonmarcos.mediacenter across all 863 source files, so this is our code now, not a fork we rebase. upstream_repo and pinned_tag stay as PROVENANCE ONLY - re-running materialize-fork against them would clobber the rename, and there is no reason to: divergence is the point. Apache-2.0 attribution is preserved in LICENSE, UPSTREAM-README.md and NOTICE.md, which owning the code does not change. The forks.<key> block itself is retained because ship-cloud-gallery.yml reads `.forks|keys[0]` and build-fork carries the signing + identity-assert path; on a vendored tree with no .git that engine is simply 'run this gradle task and sign it'.
gallery._doc_rename: Renamed: package/namespace, the baselineprofile module (com.dot.baselineprofile), the staging ContentProvider authority (com.dot.staging.*), and the Room schema directory, which is named after the @Database FQN. The authority rename also removes a real hazard: authorities are device-global, so ours colliding with genuine ReFra's meant INSTALL_FAILED_CONFLICTING_PROVIDER if both were ever installed.

release._doc: Per-APK distribution, same data-driven pattern as ac_cloud-ide::release / ac_cloud-mail::release. {sha} → git short sha, {version_name} → android.version_name.

abis._doc: ABI build axis. arm64-v8a is the device default; x86_64 covers Waydroid/emulator debugging (mirrors ac_cloud-ide::release.abis).

ghcr._doc: ORAS push as an OCI artifact (APK is a blob, not a container). Mirrors ac_cloud-ide::release.ghcr shape.

gh_release._doc: Rolling GH release 'latest', overwritten every main push, mirrors ac_cloud-ide::release.gh_release and ac_cloud-mail's shared rolling release pattern so /releases/latest/download/cloud-gallery.apk stays stable. Consumed by aa_cloud-superapp ui.external_apps[cloud-gallery].install_apk_url once wired there.

variants._doc: 2026-08-31: the two-job ABI matrix (COMMS_BUNDLE_ABI=arm64-v8a|x86_64) both resolved to the single fixed gh_release.asset_name above and uploaded with --clobber, so whichever job finished last silently overwrote the other's asset under the same public name — arm64 phones ended up installing the x86_64 build and failed with INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS. Mirrors ac_cloud-termux::release.variants, id matches COMMS_BUNDLE_ABI directly (this app has no separate CLOUDNAV_VARIANT-style short id).

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

ui._doc: THE navigation declaration (libs:bottomnav's NavDecl), the same shape every app on the shared nav bars carries. app/build.gradle.kts bakes ui.bottom_nav + ui.sections + ui.default_section into BuildConfig and shell/GalleryDeclarations.kt is their only reader. bottom_nav is the owner's order: Screenshots, Downloads, Camera (MediaStore buckets), Home (overview), Timeline (all photos by date with filters; opens on the Camera folder), Maps (photos on a map by EXIF GPS; photos without a position are the second page) and Objects (faces, scenes, text, documents; on-device index with a status). Maps and Objects carry the second row. Icons are libs:ui-icons names.

aliases._doc: #1910 Timeline was renamed All. The old ids keep working: sections.timeline -> all (stored section ids), routes.timeline_screen -> all_screen (the persisted last screen). shell/GalleryAliases is the Kotlin side; GalleryTabsTest holds the two together.

tests._doc: JVM unit tests (app/src/test): timeline filters (Camera default, persistence), geo split and clustering, index state, tab declaration. gradlew is used directly by the test engine; the debug variant needs no signing key.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Your photos by time, place and what is in them
about.description: Cloud Gallery is the photo and video gallery of the fleet, forked from an open-source MediaStore gallery. Beyond albums it has a timeline of every photo, a map of photos by place, and on-device recognition of faces, scenes, text and documents — recognition runs on the phone through the fleet's image engine, never in a cloud service. It exists so personal photos are browsed and searched without handing them to a third party.
features: All: every photo and video by date, with source and folder filters
Home source selector: Emulated, External, App
Group by kind (GIF, Images, Videos) on Screenshots, Downloads and Camera
On-device faces, scenes, text and documents
Screenshots and downloads as their own albums

screens.name: All
screens.what: Every photo by date, from all sources and folders; filter by source and folder.

guide: Grant Photos and Videos so the gallery can read them.
Use All to scroll every photo by date.
Open Maps to find photos by place.
Open Objects to search by what is in a photo.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. Photos never leave the phone: face, scene and text recognition run on the phone through the fleet's image engine. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback.
about.credits: Upstream: ReFra / Gallery by IacobIonut01 (github.com/IacobIonut01/ReFra), Apache-2.0. The fleet build adds the timeline, the map and on-device recognition, plus the fleet's update, crash and configs libraries.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
